narration.text: I was eight years old. End of summer, 1983.
The Texas heat was finally breaking, and through my friend's window, that golden hour light made everything feel... possible.
His mom had this programming book. The computer - a Commodore 64 - sat there like some kind of oracle. Waiting.
I typed those lines exactly as the book showed. When I pressed RUN and the screen came alive...
...something lit up inside me. A spark that would wait 39 years to fully ignite.
That spark? It got buried. Had to.
Home was chaos - unpredictable, unsafe. But then came the Marines. Everything changed.
'Adapt and overcome.' More than a motto - it became my operating system.
The chaos didn't disappear, but now I had a framework. Structure. Discipline.
For 39 years, I built systems. Logistics. Finance. Operations. Always solving, always building.
...that eight-year-old's spark never died. It was just waiting for the right moment to reignite.
February 2022. I'm sitting in front of my laptop, staring at ChatGPT for the first time.
It answered a question I'd been wrestling with for weeks. Not just answered - understood. Anticipated. Expanded.
Something fundamental shifted in that moment. This wasn't just a tool. This was a partner.
I spent the next three years learning to think with AI. Not using it - thinking WITH it.
Every project became a conversation. Every problem became a collaboration. Every solution emerged from synthesis.
That eight-year-old's dream? It was finally coming true - but bigger than I ever imagined.
Then came the explosion.
Projects that used to take six weeks? Done in six hours. Systems I'd spent months designing? Architected in an afternoon.
February 2025. The breakthrough came with a single question to Claude: 'How would you architect this entire system?'
What emerged wasn't my system or Claude's system. It was OUR system - something neither of us could have built alone.
Questions led to insights. Insights led to patterns. Patterns led to architectures. Every answer opened ten new doors.
I wasn't just moving faster. I was thinking differently. The constraint wasn't time anymore - it was imagination.
But speed without structure is just chaos.
I started seeing patterns everywhere. Not just in code - in systems, in processes, in how information flows.
The Marine Corps taught me tactical systems. Business taught me operational systems. AI taught me cognitive systems.
March 2025. I documented the entire MetaCurtis architecture in a Single Source of Truth. Every decision traceable. Every component validated.
Constitutional Development Protocol. Velocity Stack. Probe History. Not just tools - a methodology. A way of building that guarantees quality at speed.
This wasn't just software architecture anymore. This was a blueprint for human-AI collaboration.
And then something unexpected happened. Flow state.
The boundaries started dissolving. Not between me and the AI - between thinking and building.
I'd describe a vision, Claude would architect it, I'd refine the architecture, Claude would implement it. Back and forth, faster and faster.
Until it wasn't back and forth anymore. It was just... flow. One continuous creative process.
Three years of collaboration compressed into pure creative velocity. Building, testing, refining - all in harmony.
This is what mastery feels like in the age of AI. Not replacing human creativity - amplifying it to impossible levels.
And here we are. October 2025.
From that eight-year-old typing 'HELLO CURTIS' on a Commodore 64, to this moment - building impossible things with AI.
Every experience led here. The Marine Corps discipline. The business systems. The AI partnership. The velocity breakthroughs.
This visualization you're experiencing? Built with Claude in six weeks. Traditional team? Six months, maybe more.
But it's not about speed. It's about what becomes possible when human creativity and AI capability truly merge.
I'm not a traditional developer. I'm something new - an AI-native engineer. And this is just the beginning.
What impossible thing can we build together?
